From cc71d37fd1f11e0495b1cf580909ebea37eaa886 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dmitry Torokhov <dmitry.torokhov@gmail.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Feb 2022 17:18:58 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] HID: vivaldi: fix sysfs attributes leak

The driver creates the top row map sysfs attribute in input_configured()
method; unfortunately we do not have a callback that is executed when HID
interface is unbound, thus we are leaking these sysfs attributes, for
example when device is disconnected.

To fix it let's switch to managed version of adding sysfs attributes which
will ensure that they are destroyed when the driver is unbound.

Fixes: 14c9c014babe ("HID: add vivaldi HID driver")
Signed-off-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dmitry.torokhov@gmail.com>
Tested-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org>
Reviewed-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org>
Signed-off-by: Jiri Kosina <jkosina@suse.cz>

diff --git a/drivers/hid/hid-vivaldi.c b/drivers/hid/hid-vivaldi.c
index efa6140915f4..42ceb2058a09 100644
--- a/drivers/hid/hid-vivaldi.c
+++ b/drivers/hid/hid-vivaldi.c
@@ -144,7 +144,7 @@ static void vivaldi_feature_mapping(struct hid_device *hdev,
 static int vivaldi_input_configured(struct hid_device *hdev,
 				    struct hid_input *hidinput)
 {
-	return sysfs_create_group(&hdev->dev.kobj, &input_attribute_group);
+	return devm_device_add_group(&hdev->dev, &input_attribute_group);
 }
 
 static const struct hid_device_id vivaldi_table[] = {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/hid/hid-vivaldi.c`**
- The function `vivaldi_input_configured` has been modified. 
- The line that previously called `sysfs_create_group` to create a sysfs attribute group has been replaced with a call to `devm_device_add_group`. 

### Relationships
- The change addresses a memory leak issue by switching from a manual sysfs attribute creation to a managed version. This ensures that the sysfs attributes are automatically cleaned up when the HID device is unbound, preventing leaks when the device is disconnected. The modification is directly related to the management of sysfs attributes in the context of device lifecycle management.

Fixes: 14c9c014babe ("HID: add vivaldi HID driver")
Signed-off-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dmitry.torokhov@gmail.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug is caused by the lack of a callback to remove sysfs attributes when the HID interface is unbound, leading to a memory leak when the device is disconnected. The original implementation used `sysfs_create_group`, which does not automatically manage the lifecycle of the created attributes, resulting in them persisting even after the device is no longer present.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int vivaldi_input_configured(struct hid_device *hdev,
 				    struct hid_input *hidinput)
 {
-	return sysfs_create_group(&hdev->dev.kobj, &input_attribute_group);
+	return devm_device_add_group(&hdev->dev, &input_attribute_group);
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
return sysfs_create_group(&hdev->dev.kobj, &input_attribute_group);
```
Reason:
The use of `sysfs_create_group` does not manage the lifecycle of the created sysfs attributes, meaning that when the HID interface is unbound (e.g., when the device is disconnected), there is no mechanism to automatically remove these attributes, leading to a memory leak.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
return devm_device_add_group(&hdev->dev, &input_attribute_group);
```
Reason:
The use of `devm_device_add_group` ensures that the sysfs attributes are automatically removed when the driver is unbound, thus preventing the memory leak that occurs when the device is disconnected. This managed version of adding sysfs attributes handles their lifecycle appropriately.
